name: Floor basics
description: Moves that work on any dance floor, to any beat. Start here.

name: Goth
description: Slow, fluid and theatrical. The body sways, the arms tell the story, and the floor is never rushed.
why: A lot of goth tracks run at a normal club tempo, but the dancing sits on every other beat. Moving in half time is what gives it that drifting, unhurried look.

groove.name: Post-punk groove: floor toms and a driving bass

name: Industrial
description: Heavy, grounded and percussive. Stomps, marches and punchy arms that hit the beat hard.

groove.name: EBM groove: rolling sequencer bass and a hard clap

name: Cybergoth
description: Big, sharp and tireless. Industrial stomps and sweeping arms at hard trance speed, made to be seen across a UV-lit floor.
why: Cybergoth dancing is what happens when industrial stomping meets rave tempo. The arms do most of the work in big, clean shapes, so it reads from far away, even through goggles and falls.

groove.name: Cyber groove: hard kick, rolling bass and a stabbing lead

name: Shuffle basics
description: A slow way in to shuffling. Small drills that split the running man, the T-step and the Charleston into pieces you can learn one at a time.
why: Shuffling looks fast, but every move is two or three simple pieces stuck to the beat. Learn each piece here at 100 to 110 BPM, then take the full move to the Rave tab at club speed.

groove.name: Bounce groove: offbeat hats and a jumping bass

name: Rave
description: Light on the feet, bouncy and repetitive. Built to last for hours on a crowded floor.

groove.name: Rave groove: four on the floor and an acid line

name: House
description: Grounded and bouncy, with the groove in the chest. Quick, light footwork comes and goes on top of the jack.
why: House dancing grew up in the clubs of Chicago and New York. Everything sits on the jack, a bounce that lives in the chest rather than the knees, so once that's going any step looks like house.

groove.name: House groove: offbeat hats, organ bass and seventh chords

name: Vogue
description: Fierce, precise and posed. Catwalk, hands and poses from ballroom culture, scaled for a club floor.
why: Vogue comes from the Black and Latinx queer ballroom scene in New York. It's danced as a performance: every move is meant to be seen, and hitting a pose on the music matters more than doing a lot.

groove.name: Ballroom groove: four on the floor and the "ha" crash
